ui-access.external.fingerprint: SHA-256 fingerprint of the self-signed certificate: {fingerprint}
ui-access.external.fingerprintHint: When the browser says the certificate is not trusted, look at the certificate's SHA-256 and continue only if it matches this one ({command} access show prints it too).
ui-access.external.hint: Off by default. Turning it on widens who can connect, so it needs the PIN; once on, opening the page always takes a one-time passcode. TLS (a self-signed certificate) by default; plain HTTP is allowed only on overlay-network or LAN addresses, and browsers treat a plain-HTTP page as an insecure origin (see docs/WEB-ORIGINS.md).
ui-access.external.link: Make a link to open from another machine…
ui-access.external.linkPinWhy: Whoever gets this link can open the page as you over the network.
ui-access.external.pinWhy: Turning on or changing the outside face widens who can connect.
ui-access.external.title: Outside face (open this page from other machines)
ui-access.link.noUrl: No link: type this passcode on the other machine:
ui-access.link.open: Open it in a browser on the other machine:
ui-access.local.line: Listens only on the loopback address{url}{source}.
ui-access.local.title: Local face
ui-access.origins.addPinWhy: A listed page can use a token an external issuer gave you to operate this {product} as you in the browser.
ui-access.origins.empty: None (external UIs in a browser cannot connect).
ui-access.origins.externalOff: The outside face is off now, so the list is not used for the time being.
ui-access.origins.hint: Only on the outside face: a listed page can use a token an external issuer signed for you to operate this {product} as you from a browser, through the outside face; the local face accepts no other origin. A UI backend in a server process does not need this. Adding one needs the PIN; removing the last one or clearing all does not. Write https://host[:port]; http:// is allowed only for loopback (development).
ui-access.origins.removePinWhy: Changing the allowed external UI origins needs the PIN (the whole list is replaced).
ui-access.origins.title: Allowed external UI origins (external UIs in a browser)
ui-access.passcode.hint: The passcode decides who can open this page; the PIN decides who can let others in. They are separate. auto: on when other people have accounts on this machine or the outside face is on. Now {state}{shared}. Changing it needs the PIN.
ui-access.passcode.pinWhy: Changing the passcode may widen who can open this page.
ui-access.passcode.title: Passcode
ui-access.portSource.moved: the preferred one was taken, a temporary one
ui-access.relay.acme: Get a certificate from a certificate authority (Let's Encrypt by default, which means agreeing to its subscriber agreement; turned off, only {product} instances can use the relay to reach you)
ui-access.relay.hint: {product} connects out to the relay and stays connected, getting a fixed outside address that goes on your identity card. The relay only forwards encrypted bytes and cannot see the content; requests coming through it reach only the outside face, which does not need to be listening first. Choosing and turning off both need the PIN.
ui-access.relay.offPinWhy: Once the relay is turned off, people on other networks can no longer call you.
ui-access.relay.setPinWhy: With a relay chosen, anyone who can reach the relay can knock on the outside face's door.
ui-access.relay.title: Relay (agents on other networks can call you even behind a router)
ui-access.title: Faces and passcode
